This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with interdependent values (common value + private taste). In a standard second-price auction with private values, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy. However, with common value components, the "winner's curse" can occur. But since the common value is additive and the taste adjustment is also additive, and I am bidding against only two others, bidding slightly below or at my value is generally optimal. Given my value is $27 (moderate to high), I will bid my true value to maximize the probability of winning profitably.
